sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Chemerin competition binding assay in L1.2 transfectants: HA-tagged huCCRL2 and mCCRL2 bound His8-chemerin and competed with untagged chemerin, confirming surface display and ligand-binding function fully preserved.
sites.rationale: CCRL2 has no signal peptide; the extracellular N-terminus spans residues 1–39 (39 aa before TM1 at residue 40), providing ample room for a short tag. The paper reports an N-terminal HA tag on full-length, membrane-anchored huCCRL2 with no residue number stated; because the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this GPCR, the junction is unambiguously insert_after_residue=0 (topology_derived). Python confirms residue_after = M (seq[0]). Chemerin binding was preserved, qualifying this as surface_and_function. L6/L7 (PMC2556791): coding regions of mCCRL2 and huCCRL2 cloned with an engineered N-terminal HA tag into pcDNA3 as full-length, membrane-anchored receptors; expressed in L1.2 transfectants. No specific junction residue is named; CCRL2 has no annotated signal peptide (UniProt Q9Y4X3), so the extracellular N-terminus begins at M1 and the tag prepends before it.

sources.claim: Various concentrations of untagged serum form chemerin were incubated with mCCRL2-HA, huCCRL2-HA, mCRTH2-HA, or mCMKLR1-HA L1.2 transfectants in the presence of 10 nM His 8 -tagged serum form chemerin.

After 2 weeks, cells were detached and sorted for receptor expression as described in Section “ Flow Cytometry and Cell Sorting .”

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines describe N-terminal tags on full-length, membrane-anchored CCRL2; none describes an internal loop insertion or a C-terminal extracellular tag. CCRL2 has no annotated signal peptide (UniProt Q9Y4X3), so the extracellular N-terminus begins at M1 and insert_after_residue=0 is the correct prepend junction. L5 describes C-terminal truncations of mCCRL2 (at mouse residues 310A and 319F) used to probe helix-VIII trafficking; these are intracellular truncation endpoints, not tag insertion sites, and are recorded in other_positions. No internal ECL (ECL1 96–104, ECL2 170–198, ECL3 261–282) or C-terminal extracellular tag insertion is supported by any ledger line.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal truncation endpoint of mCCRL2 H8− construct (mouse 310A, human residue 310 Y); lies within the intracellular C-terminus (304–344) and was used to study helix-VIII role in receptor trafficking, not as a tag insertion site.
